# osc_my_app (Resource)

Manages a My App: your own application, built from a git repository and run on Web Runner.

On every build the platform clones the repository, then runs `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm start` (or the equivalent for the runtime) from the repository root, or from `sub_path`. The app must listen on the `PORT` it is given. Environment variables come from the bound parameter store (`config_service`); manage the store with `osc_parameter_store` and its values with `osc_parameter`.

Terraform manages the app, not its releases: pushing to the tracked branch does not redeploy. Change `source_ref` to deploy a tag, or change `rebuild_trigger` to rebuild from the current head.

Attach a custom domain with `osc_domain`, using `domain_service_id` and `id` of this resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A Node.js API built from a private GitHub repository, with its environment from a
# parameter store. Changing rebuild_trigger (here, from CI) deploys the head of main.
resource "osc_my_app" "api" {
  name           = "myapi"
  type           = "nodejs"
  git_url        = "https://github.com/example/my-api"
  source_ref     = "main"
  git_credential = "github-example"
  config_service = osc_parameter_store.api.name

  high_availability = true
  rebuild_trigger   = var.release_sha

  # The app reads its environment at start, so create the values first.
  depends_on = [osc_parameter.node_env, osc_parameter.database_url]
}

output "api_url" {
  value = osc_my_app.api.url
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `git_url` (String) HTTPS URL of the git repository, on any host (GitHub, OSC managed Gitea, GitLab, ...), without a `#ref`. Changing it replaces the app.
- `name` (String) App name, unique within the workspace. Changing it replaces the app.

### Optional

- `config_api_key` (String, Sensitive) API key of the parameter store, needed to decrypt its secret values. When unset it is read from the parameter store, which is what you want unless the key was rotated outside Terraform.
- `config_service` (String) Name of the parameter store whose values become the app's environment variables. Changing it rebinds the app with a rolling restart.
- `git_credential` (String) Name of a git credential stored in the workspace, used instead of `git_token` so that the token never passes through Terraform. Conflicts with `git_token`.
- `git_token` (String, Sensitive) Access token for a private repository. Conflicts with `git_credential`.
- `high_availability` (Boolean) Run a standby instance so that rebuilds are blue-green deployments with no downtime. Only for `nodejs` and `python` apps, and only on paid plans.
- `rebuild_trigger` (String) Any value. Changing it rebuilds the app from the head of `source_ref` with a fresh image, for example a commit SHA or a release version from CI. For an app with `high_availability` the rebuild is a blue-green deployment.
- `source_ref` (String) Branch or tag to build. Commit SHAs are not supported; tag the commit instead. Changing it deploys that ref with a rolling restart. When unset the app builds the default branch, and the ref the platform reports is kept in state.
- `sub_path` (String) Directory within the repository to build and start from, for monorepos. Note that the platform does not load the parameter store for an app with a `sub_path`; the app must fetch it itself from `APP_CONFIG_URL`. Changing it replaces the app.
- `type` (String) Runtime: `nodejs`, `python`, `wasm`, `golang` or `dotnet`. Changing it replaces the app.
- `wait_for_ready` (Boolean) Wait for the build to finish after create and after any change that restarts the app, up to fifteen minutes, and fail if the build fails.

### Read-Only

- `build_status` (String) Status of the latest build: `building`, `running`, `failed` or `unknown`.
- `domain_service_id` (String) The `service_id` to use in an `osc_domain` for this app, together with `id` as `instance_name`.
- `id` (String) The app id, which the platform derives from the name. Use it with `terraform import`.
- `managed_domain` (String) The hostname the platform assigns the app, `<hash>.apps.osaas.io`. Empty until assigned.
- `url` (String) The app's URL on the Web Runner host.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import osc_my_app.api myapi
```
